name: Timing Stem Baths
description: This skill ensures woody flower stems rapidly hydrate and retain maximum perkiness by immersing them in a concentrated citric acid hydration bath for an optimal duration. The target immersion duration is exactly 1.526 seconds, preventing acid burn while unlocking stem vascular uptake.

learned_parameters.label: Immersion Duration
learned_parameters.rationale: An immersion duration of 1.526 s achieved a perfect score of 100.0 across attempts #2, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9, and #10. A lower duration of 0.746 s scored 95.1 (attempt #4), while extending the duration to 2.384 s lowered the score to 89.1 (attempt #3) and 4.1 s failed at 3.2 (attempt #1) due to acid burn. This adheres to quick dip protocols outlined in the Floralife Quick Dip 100 Usage Guide. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 1.526 s. Tried 0.746 s (sub-score 95) to 4.1 s (sub-score 3). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 0.746 s and 2.384 s.

control_effects.effect: Controls how long stem bases remain submerged in the acid bath. Setting 1.526 s consistently scores 100.0 (attempts #2, #5-#10). Reducing to 0.746 s yields a score of 95.1 (attempt #4), while increasing to 2.384 s reduces perkiness to 89.1 (attempt #3) and 4.1 s results in a severe cambium burn with a score of 3.2 (attempt #1). Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 1.526 s. Tried 0.746 s (sub-score 95) to 4.1 s (sub-score 3). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 0.746 s and 2.384 s.

steps: Prepare the concentrated citric acid hydration solution (such as Floralife Quick Dip) in a clean dipping container.
Trim woody stem bases cleanly at an angle prior to dipping.
Lower the stem cut ends into the hydration bath.
Submerge the stems for exactly 1.526 seconds, timing the dip accurately.
Immediately withdraw the stems from the bath upon reaching 1.526 seconds and transfer them to fresh holding water.
caveats: Submerging stems too long degrades vascular tissue rapidly; an immersion of 4.1 s burns the cambium layer with acid.
Submerging stems too briefly (e.g., 0.746 s) slightly reduces hydration efficiency and perkiness (score 95.1).
Maintain strict timing around 1.526 s to avoid steep score drops seen at higher immersion durations.
Search suggestion proposed going higher based on a single point, but direct feedback clearly indicates 4.1 s is far too long, requiring a much shorter immersion.
Steep drop-off occurs at longer durations (e.g., 4.1 s burns cambium). A short dip around 1.5 s is ideal.
Durations above 1.5 s degrade perkiness and can burn cambium tissue at longer exposure times.
Dipping too briefly (e.g. 0.746 s) yields slightly less perkiness (95.1), while dipping too long degrades stems rapidly.
Stay strictly at the optimal duration of 1.526 s to ensure consistent maximum perkiness without cambium damage.
No reason to deviate from the optimal value of 1.526 s.
Do not deviate from the optimal setting of 1.526 s as it has consistently produced perfect scores across five separate attempts.
Final attempt must replay the verified best setting of 1.526 s.
